notes: Read all 131 source lines (numbered) before editing. The hook paints an unread-count badge onto the browser tab favicon via document `<link rel="icon">` lookup, `<canvas>` compositing and `new Image()` loading — browser-only behaviour with no React Native analog (a native binary has no browser tab/favicon; the OS app-icon badge is a separate API and not this hook's contract). Ported faithfully behind a native-safe DOM facade gate per the InstallPrompt/useConfirm 'prefer globalThis.* when present, else explicit unavailable state' convention.
L1 `import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react'` -> `import {useEffect, useRef} from 'react'` (react is RN-compatible; native prettier drops inner-brace spacing).

L2 `import { useUnreadCount } from '@/api/hooks/useNotifications'` -> `from '../api/hooks/useNotifications'` (native parity path; same hook, `select: data => data?.count ?? 0` so `data` is a number, keeping `const {data: count = 0}` and the `/notifications/unread-count` API intent).

L3 `import { useSettings } from '@/hooks/useSettings'` -> native `from '../api/hooks/useSettings'`. The web app-level `@/hooks/useSettings` (which returns `{ settings }` merged with defaults) is not yet ported; the native api hook returns `useQuery<AppSettings>`, so `const { settings } = useSettings(); settings.tab_badge_enabled` (L27-28) is adapted to `const {data: settings} = useSettings(); settings?.tab_badge_enabled !== false`. Semantics are identical: web defaults tab_badge_enabled to true, and `undefined !== false` is also true, so `enabled` defaults to true and is only false when the setting is explicitly false. `/settings` API intent preserved.
L5-9 constants ported verbatim: FAVICON_SIZE = 32, BADGE_COLOR = '#f87171' (the red-400 'needs attention' comment kept byte-for-byte), BADGE_TEXT_COLOR = '#ffffff'. Visual intent preserved.

L11-24 hook JSDoc carried over (paint coloured dot + optional count, restore on zero/disable, mutate every `<link rel="icon">`, progressive-enhancement no-op on image load failure) with one added sentence noting that on a pure native runtime there is no favicon surface so the hook is an inert no-op (nativeFaviconBadgeCapabilities).

L25-30 hook signature `export function useFaviconBadge(): void` and all four locals preserved with the same names: count (L26), enabled (L28), originalsRef (L29, Map keyed by the favicon link element), seqRef (L30). The Map key type HTMLLinkElement became the locally-declared FaviconLinkElement facade ({href: string; dataset: {baseHref?: string}}) since the RN tsconfig lib excludes `dom`.

L32-37 main effect open + DOM presence guard: web `if (typeof document === 'undefined') return` (L33) became `const doc = getFaviconDocument(); if (!doc) return`, where getFaviconDocument() returns react-native-web's `globalThis.document` when it exposes querySelectorAll and undefined on a pure native runtime — the same early-return no-op. `document.querySelectorAll<HTMLLinkElement>('link[rel="icon"]')` -> `doc.querySelectorAll('link[rel="icon"]')` (facade returns ArrayLike, Array.from preserved), and the `links.length === 0` early return (L37) is kept verbatim.

L39-57 original-href snapshot + useDynamicAppIcon coordination ported 1:1 including the full comment: for each link, `link.dataset.baseHref` (liveBase) re-snapshots into originalsRef, else snapshot `link.href` once when not already present.
L59-69 `restore()` closure and the `if (!enabled || count <= 0) { restore(); return }` clear path ported verbatim (restore writes each link's snapshotted href back).

L71-78 stale-onload sequence guard ported 1:1: `const seq = ++seqRef.current`, `firstLink = links[0]`, `orig = originalsRef.current.get(firstLink)`, `if (!orig) return`, including the explanatory comment.

L79-118 image-load + canvas compositing ported faithfully against the facade. `new Image()` (L79) became `const ImageCtor = getImageConstructor(); if (!ImageCtor) return; const img = new ImageCtor()` — a native-safety guard that is a no-op on the web target where Image always exists alongside document. img.crossOrigin/onload/onerror/src, the seq re-check, `document.createElement('canvas')` -> `doc.createElement('canvas')`, width/height = FAVICON_SIZE, getContext('2d') null-guard, drawImage, the BADGE_COLOR arc dot (arc(FAVICON_SIZE-8, 8, 7, 0, Math.PI*2)), the `count < 10` single-digit fillText (bold 11px system-ui font, center/middle), `canvas.toDataURL('image/png')`, the `for (const link of links) link.href = dataUrl` fan-out, and both the empty-with-comment catch (tainted canvas / jsdom) and onerror handlers are preserved exactly. CanvasRenderingContext2D / HTMLCanvasElement / HTMLImageElement became the local FaviconCanvasContext / FaviconCanvasElement / FaviconImage facade interfaces.

L119 dependency array `[count, enabled]` preserved. L121-130 unmount-restore effect ported 1:1: `const originals = originalsRef.current` captured first (satisfies react-hooks/exhaustive-deps), cleanup restores every captured link.href; `[]` deps preserved.

Browser-only state made explicit: exported `nativeFaviconBadgeCapabilities` { faviconLinkElementsAvailable: false, canvasBadgeRenderingAvailable: false } documents the pure-native-runtime reality (no favicon to badge); the favicon path still executes on the react-native-web target where a real DOM is present, so genuine parity is retained there. No DOM elements, Recharts, Leaflet, or web UI components are imported.
Gates run from apps/native: npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit); npm run lint -- --quiet; npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles.
